subject: Taxes
title: The Women's Tax Riot in Nigeria
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Women's Tax Riot in Nigeria.

hook.text: In 1929, 10,000 Igbo women marched against British tax collectors in Nigeria.

buildup.text: British officials counted women and livestock—a signal that a new tax was coming.

discovery.text: Women surrounded government offices, danced, sang protest songs, and demanded the removal of corrupt warrant chiefs.

twist.text: British soldiers fired on unarmed women, killing over 50.

climax.text: The Women's War proved that tax resistance isn't always about money—it's about dignity and power.

punchline.text: 10,000 women vs. an empire. Nigeria's tax war changed colonial rule.

quiz.question: What triggered the Women's War in Nigeria?
options: A new tax on women who had never been taxed
